definitions.explanation: The central part of the body excluding the head and limbs; in fitness, the deep muscles of the torso that support posture and movement.

examples.japanese: {体幹|たいかん}を{鍛|きた}えるとバランスが{良|よ}くなる。
{体幹|たいかん}トレーニングは{毎日|まいにち}{続|つづ}けることが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It's important to do core training every day.

examples.japanese: プロの{選手|せんしゅ}は{体幹|たいかん}がしっかりしているから、{当|あ}たり{負|ま}けしない。
examples.english: Professional athletes have strong cores, so they don't get knocked off balance by contact.

notes:
USAGE:
{体幹|たいかん} has become a widely used fitness term in Japan. It refers to the trunk muscles (abdominals, back, pelvis, diaphragm) that stabilize the body. The term gained popularity through sports science and fitness media.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {体幹|たいかん}トレーニング (core training)
- {体幹|たいかん}を{鍛|きた}える (to train/strengthen the core)
- {体幹|たいかん}が{強|つよ}い (to have a strong core)
- {体幹|たいかん}が{弱|よわ}い (to have a weak core)

RELATED WORDS:
- インナーマッスル (inner muscles — often used interchangeably in casual speech)
- {腹筋|ふっきん} (abdominal muscles — one component of the core)
